name: Internally Tested Tamil Chicken Dum Biryani

ingredients.name: Rock salt
ingredients.note: calibrated reference; adjust only after a controlled retest

ingredients.name: Hot water
ingredients.note: measure rice and water with the same tumbler; this is the total water retained in the biryani

steps.instruction: Measure the dry rice by volume and separately reserve hot water equal to 1.5 times that volume. Wash and soak the rice for 30 minutes. While it soaks, finish all cutting, grinding and ingredient measurement. Do not parboil the rice yet.
steps.checkpoint: Rice has soaked for 30 minutes; recipe water is measured separately; all ingredients and both cooking pots are ready.
steps.warning: The reserved 1.5-ratio water is recipe water and must not be used for parboiling. Rice will be half-cooked later while the chicken gravy approaches readiness.

steps.stage: Fry whole spices, garlic and ginger
steps.instruction: Heat the groundnut oil in the tri-ply biryani pot. Fry cinnamon, cardamom and cloves until aromatic. Add ground garlic and cook until golden and aromatic. Add ground ginger and cook until its raw smell disappears.
steps.checkpoint: Garlic is golden—not dark brown—and both garlic and ginger smell cooked and aromatic.
steps.warning: Garlic can turn bitter quickly. Reduce heat and move immediately to the next ingredient if it darkens too fast.

steps.instruction: Add onion, tomato, mint and coriander. Cook until the vegetables collapse into a cohesive gravy with no raw tomato smell or firm onion pieces.
steps.checkpoint: Thick, cohesive onion-tomato gravy; softened pieces; no raw smell; no watery pool.
steps.warning: Stir often enough to prevent the concentrated base from catching.

steps.instruction: Add chilli powder and rock salt. Add curd and cook until its raw smell disappears and the gravy comes together again.
steps.checkpoint: Curd is fully incorporated, the raw sour smell is gone, and the gravy looks cohesive rather than split and watery.
steps.warning: Control the heat and stir the bottom so the curd and masala do not stick.

steps.stage: Coordinate chicken gravy and half-cooked rice
steps.instruction: Add chicken to the biryani pot and cook for about 10 minutes, stirring periodically, until a proper gravy forms and the chicken is nearly cooked. When the rice-water task below is ready, add lemon juice and 50–60% of the reserved recipe water to the chicken gravy. Put the tawa on the stove and the biryani pot on it. Use high heat only until bubbles appear across the gravy, then immediately reduce to low.
steps.checkpoint: Chicken is nearly cooked; the formed gravy is actively bubbling across the pot on the tawa; heat has been reduced to low; the separately drained rice is simultaneously at about 50% doneness.
steps.warning: Move between pots in short, deliberate actions—do not stir both at once. Never add rice to merely warm gravy, and never leave either pot unattended on high heat.

parallelTasks.name: Second pot — parboil rice
parallelTasks.startWhen: Immediately after adding chicken to the gravy pot, place a second pot of excess water on another burner over high heat.
parallelTasks.instruction: Continue checking and stirring the chicken between visits to the second pot. Add the soaked rice only when the second pot is at a rolling boil and the chicken gravy is roughly 5–7 minutes from readiness. Boil rice for 5–7 minutes, test a grain, then drain and discard all parboiling water.
parallelTasks.readyWhen: Rice holds its long shape; the outside is partly cooked; the centre is firm and opaque; pressing breaks it but does not mash it.
parallelTasks.ifReadyEarly: Drain immediately. Keep it covered for no more than a brief 1–2 minute wait while bringing the gravy to an active boil; never leave it sitting in hot water.

steps.instruction: Place the drained 50%-cooked rice over the boiling gravy. Use a spoon or ladle only to gently reposition portions so rice settles into the gravy; do not stir or fold from the bottom. Pour the remaining 40–50% of the reserved recipe water evenly over the rice.
steps.checkpoint: A little gravy rises through portions of the rice and gives the surface light patches of colour. Rice is neither completely flooded nor completely dry and white.
steps.warning: Aggressive mixing breaks the long grains and damages the target texture. Total retained recipe water across both additions must equal 1.5 times the original dry-rice volume.

steps.instruction: Close the lid tightly. Keep the pot on the tawa over low heat for 20 minutes. Do not open or stir during dum.
steps.checkpoint: Gentle steam and biryani aroma with no burnt smell. The pot remains tightly closed for the complete 20 minutes.
steps.warning: The supported home method uses a tight lid and bottom tawa only. Do not place improvised fire, charcoal or hot material on the lid.

steps.instruction: Switch off the heat and rest unopened for 10 minutes. Open away from your face. Verify the thickest chicken piece reaches 74°C/165°F away from bone. Transfer the biryani gently into a large second vessel, lifting sections so the concentrated bottom gravy and oil combine with the lighter top rice. Stop once evenly distributed.
steps.checkpoint: Long separate grains, evenly distributed colour and oil, formed gravy coating the rice, and chicken at a safe temperature.
steps.warning: Do not stir in circles or scrape burnt material from the bottom. If chicken is below 74°C/165°F, use the separate-pan recovery; do not continue cooking the entire rice pot blindly.

recoveryRules.action: Turn off the heat. Remove black garlic immediately and assess whether the oil smells bitter. If the oil is bitter, discard it and restart this stage; otherwise add the next ingredient promptly and continue on lower heat.
recoveryRules.safetyNote: Do not add water to hot oil.

recoveryRules.action: Reduce heat immediately and move the unstuck gravy to a clean pot without scraping the burnt base. Continue only if the transferred gravy does not taste or smell bitter.
recoveryRules.safetyNote: Handle the hot pot and oil carefully.

recoveryRules.action: Before adding the measured recipe water or rice, simmer uncovered while stirring regularly until a formed gravy returns. Reassess moisture before continuing.

Drain immediately and spread on a wide tray to stop carry-over cooking. This batch is at high risk of breaking; handle minimally and shorten dum only after checking doneness during a controlled retest.
Confirm that all remaining measured recipe water has been distributed evenly. Do not exceed the total 1.5-times dry-rice-volume allowance without a controlled recipe retest.
Do not add more water. Keep the pot uncovered briefly on low heat only until the surface is no longer flooded, watching continuously, then close for dum.
recoveryRules.safetyNote: Do not leave the concentrated base unattended.

recoveryRules.action: Turn off the heat and move the pot to a cool surface. Do not scrape the bottom. After steam settles, transfer the unaffected upper portions to a clean vessel without disturbing the burnt base.
recoveryRules.safetyNote: Handle the hot, heavy pot carefully.

recoveryRules.problem: Chicken below safe temperature after dum
recoveryRules.action: Remove the affected chicken pieces. Cover and simmer them separately with some bottom gravy and 30–60 ml hot water if needed. Turn occasionally and cook until the thickest part reaches 74°C/165°F away from bone. Keep rice covered off heat, then return the cooked chicken and gently lift once or twice.
recoveryRules.safetyNote: Do not rely on colour alone and do not keep cooking the entire biryani pot, which can burn the gravy and damage the rice.

recoveryRules.action: Do not add more salt. Serve with unsalted plain curd; for a future controlled batch recalibrate the rock-salt quantity rather than changing it mid-session.
Do not add more chilli. Serve with plain curd. Do not add sugar directly to the biryani.
